info.title: BlueBubbles Server API
info.description:
The BlueBubbles server HTTP API.

## Versions

`/api/v1` is the surface inherited from the previous Node/Electron server. It is frozen: a bug fix belongs in v1, new capability does not.

`/api/v2` is everything this server does that the previous one did not. Its routes are individually gated; see `x-availability` on each operation, so a default-configured server serves none of them.

## Reading the payload schemas

Handlers exchange untyped JSON rather than a declared type, so a schema here describes the payloads this API is known to produce. Read one as a lower bound:

- A field typed `null` may carry a value in cases this document does not cover.
- An array with empty `items` has no described element type.
- `required` under-claims rather than over-claims: a field it does not list may still always be present.
- Where a payload could not be described unambiguously, the schema is empty rather than confidently wrong.

Some routes describe only their surface: method, path, parameters and status codes, with no payload schema.

## What is not described

A few routes describe their failures but not their success payload: those whose success needs a live call, an available update, or an attachment that has been purged to iCloud.

tags.name: find-my-v2

tags.description: Development builds only. Requires the `findMy` AND `findMyLocationSharing` feature flags, both off by default; a release server has no such routes.

tags.name: facetime-enhanced-v2
tags.description: Requires FaceTime support to be enabled. Off by default.

tags.name: facetime-incoming-v2
tags.description: Requires FaceTime support AND incoming-call hand-off. Both off by default.

tags.name: auth-v2
tags.description: Registered only when `auth_mode` is not `password`. Under the default these paths 404.

tags.name: hydration-v2
tags.description: Registered only when a non-legacy payload codec is enabled.

schema.description: Creates a conversation and answers with the whole chat: its participants, and the message the create sent. What is possible depends on the configuration — the Private API creates either kind and needs no first message; without it a ONE-TO-ONE chat is created by sending `message` through AppleScript, and a GROUP needs the user-installed Shortcut.

addresses.description: Who the conversation is with. One address makes a one-to-one chat, two or more a group.

message.description: The first message. Optional with the Private API, REQUIRED without it: there is no other way to bring a chat into existence, so a create with no message is refused with that as the reason.

method.description: `apple-script` or `private-api`. Accepted, and NOT acted on: this server chooses the backend from what it has, so naming one cannot force it. Documented because clients send it and the reference validates it.

tempGuid.description: Client-generated id echoed back on the message the create sent, so a client can match it to the row it inserted optimistically.

one-to-one.summary: A new chat with one person.
one-to-one.description: Works on every configuration. Without the Private API the chat comes into existence as a side effect of sending `message`, which is why it is here.

group.description: Needs the Private API or the installed Shortcut. A server with neither refuses this and names the setting that fixes it rather than failing generically.

value.message: Making a group for the weekend

schema.description: Pages the message table. Every field is optional: an empty body answers with the newest 100 messages across every conversation. `metadata` carries `total` (rows matching every filter, not the size of the table), `count` (rows on this page), `limit` and `offset`.

chatGuid.description: Scope the page to one conversation. A GUID that names no chat answers 200 with an empty `data` and a message naming it, which is how a client tells "no such chat" from "no messages matching".

with.description: Relations to load. Matched as substrings, so `chat`, `chats` and `chat.participants` all select the chat relation: `chat`, `chat.participants`, `attachment`, `attachment.metadata`, `attributedBody`, `messageSummaryInfo`, `payloadData`. The sending handle is always loaded and needs no entry. Ask for `attributedBody` if you render text: an outgoing message's `text` column is null on Ventura and newer and its words are in there. `attachment.metadata` opens each file off disk, so it costs a probe per attachment and is off unless asked for.

where.description: Filters, ANDed together, and applied to `metadata.total` as well as to the page. Each entry is one statement from a fixed set; a statement outside it is refused with a 400 quoting it back, never ignored. The set: `message.ROWID > :x`, `message.ROWID <= :x`, `message.is_from_me = :x` (0 or 1), `message.text LIKE :x COLLATE NOCASE` (write your own `%` wildcards), `message.guid IN (:...x)`, `message.associated_message_guid IS NULL`, `chat.guid = :x`, `handle.id = :x`.

statement.description: One of the statements listed above. Matched on shape, so spacing and the placeholder's name are yours: `message.ROWID>:since` is the same filter as `message.ROWID > :startRowId`.

args.description: The bound values, keyed by placeholder name without its colon. An empty object for a statement that binds nothing.

limit.description: Page size, 1 to 1000 inclusive. Defaults to 100.

offset.description: Rows to skip before the page. Defaults to 0.

sort.description: `DESC` for newest first, which is the default, or `ASC` for oldest first. Page a sync with `ASC` so a message arriving mid-sync cannot shift a page you have already read.

after.description: Only messages sent at or after this time, epoch MILLISECONDS. Inclusive.

before.description: Only messages sent at or before this time, epoch MILLISECONDS. Inclusive.

convertAttachments.description: Accepted and carried, but no field of this response depends on it: an attachment is converted when it is downloaded, not when a message is serialized. Defaults to true.

name.description: The sticker's own name. Messages leaves this empty for a sticker made on the Mac.

kind.description: The external URI's source, parsed for you: `emoji`, `memoji`, `user`, or `unknown` for a source this server does not recognise.

name.description: The sticker's own name. Usually null; Messages leaves it empty.

accessibility_name.description: What VoiceOver reads, e.g. `loudly crying face`. The only searchable text the store keeps, so it is what a client should filter on.

effect.description: `-1` for a plain sticker; `0` or more when an effect is applied.

created_at.description: When it entered the store, epoch MILLISECONDS.

last_used_at.description: When it was last sent, epoch MILLISECONDS.

library_index.description: The store's own ordering value within a shelf. Larger is newer, and it is what the list is sorted by; it does not always agree with `last_used_at`.

attribution_name.description: Shown on the sticker detail sheet, e.g. `Stickers`.

attribution_bundle_id.description: The balloon bundle id behind that attribution.

representations.description: Every rendition the store holds. A sticker Messages made has two: a full-size `still` and a small `keyboard` preview; an emoji sticker has one.

role.description: `com.apple.stickers.role.still`, `com.apple.stickers.role.keyboard`, or an EMPTY string for a sticker with a single rendition. Send it back as `?role=`.

uti.description: The store's uniform type identifier, e.g. `public.heic`.

mime_type.description: That UTI as a MIME type, so a client need not map it.

width.description: Width the store draws it at. Not always integral.

is_preferred.description: The rendition `:id/image` serves when no role is asked for.

oneOf.description: When the store took the sticker but this server cannot read it back: almost always a Mac that has not granted Full Disk Access. The sticker IS saved. external_uri.description: The sticker's address in the store, which is what the donation was filed under. The one identifier this response can offer that is not a lie.

byte_count.description: Size of the sticker's bytes as the store received them.

shelf.description: Always `recent`: a newly added sticker lands there. Stated rather than omitted so this shape and the full one agree about the field.

saved.description: Always true, and present only on this shape. It is how a client tells `the sticker was added but could not be read back` from a failure, the identifier is absent in both cases, and only this says the operation succeeded.

schema.description: Mutes a conversation and answers with the resulting state. THREE WAYS TO SAY WHEN, and sending none of them mutes indefinitely, which is what Messages' own Hide Alerts does and should not need a magic value.

mutedUntil.description: When the mute lifts: epoch MILLISECONDS, or an ISO 8601 string. Absolute, so a device with a skewed clock is computing the instant itself.

durationSeconds.description: How long to mute for, counted from the SERVER's clock. This is the one to send from a phone: it is what keeps a one-hour mute from arriving already expired.

indefinite.description: `true` mutes until something unmutes it, and wins over the other two. The same as sending none of them, for a client that would rather say so.

syncToPairedDevice.description: Push the change to the user's other devices. Defaults to true, which is what Messages' own toggle does.

hide-alerts.description: The common case, and the one an empty body already does. Sending `indefinite` says so out loud rather than relying on the absence of the other fields.

for-an-hour.summary: Mute for a fixed length of time.
for-an-hour.description: Relative, so the server does the arithmetic. A phone computing the instant itself is how a one-hour mute becomes one that already lapsed.

until-a-moment.description: Epoch milliseconds, matching every other timestamp on this API; an ISO 8601 string is accepted too, because half the clients that reach this server send those.

reason.description:
`no_license` — No license has ever been entered on this server.

`license_expired` — A subscription ended. `subscription_ended_at` says when, and this is the only reason that carries it.

`license_revoked` — The license was refunded, charged back, or revoked.

`tier_insufficient` — A subscription is held, but a lower tier than this route requires.

`machine_mismatch` — The entitlement was issued for a different Mac. Re-entering the key on this one fixes it, subject to the activation limit.

`validation_unavailable` — The license service could not be reached for long enough that the offline window lapsed. NOT the same as an expired subscription: nothing is known to be wrong with it, and a client that says 'your subscription expired' here is telling somebody something false about their own money.

current_tier.description: The tier this server holds, or null for none.

purchase_url.description: Where somebody without a subscription goes.

subscription_ended_at.description: Epoch MILLISECONDS, as every other date in this API. Present only with `reason: license_expired`, and ABSENT rather than null otherwise — a null or a zero invites a client to render 1970.
